data.name: Diagnosi_TetheringPubblica
data.value: With USB tethering the phone creates a new network, and Windows treats it as public: so the phone can’t see the PC. Make it private: Settings › Network & internet › Ethernet › the phone’s network › Network profile type › Private.

data.name: Diagnosi_RetePubblica
data.value: On a public network Windows hides the PC from other devices. If it’s your home or office network, make it private: Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi (or Ethernet) › your network › Network profile type › Private. Away from home, use the USB cable.

data.name: Diagnosi_FirewallManca

data.name: Guida_PrimoCollegamento1
data.value: Open WebcamLR on the PC: it makes itself visible on the network.

data.name: Guida_PrimoCollegamento2
data.value: On first launch Windows asks for network permission: allow private networks.

data.name: Guida_PrimoCollegamento3
data.value: On the phone, on the same Wi-Fi network as the PC, tap the PC’s name.

data.name: Guida_PrimoCollegamento4

data.name: Guida_QrCode1
data.value: If the PC doesn’t show up on the phone, use the QR code shown in this window.

data.name: Guida_QrCode2
data.value: On the phone, tap “Scan the computer’s QR code” and point the camera at it.

data.name: Guida_QrCode3
data.value: It’s also the safest way: the QR code contains the PC’s security code.

data.name: Guida_Comandi3

data.name: Guida_NonSiCollega1
data.value: The phone and PC must be on the same Wi-Fi network (not the “guest” one).

data.name: Guida_NonSiCollega2
data.value: The PC’s network must be “Private”: Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi › properties.

data.name: Guida_NonSiCollega3
data.value: On the iPhone: Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › WebcamLR on.

data.name: Guida_NonSiCollega4
data.value: Where the network keeps devices apart, turn on the phone’s hotspot and connect the PC to it.

data.name: Guida_NonSiCollega5
data.value: With the USB cable: plug the iPhone into the PC and open WebcamLR on both; “USB cable” appears at the top. You need the free “Apple Devices” app from the Microsoft Store. It’s the most stable connection.

data.name: Guida_NonSiCollega6
data.value: With the cable and Android: turn on “USB tethering” on the phone and connect as on Wi-Fi or with the QR code. If Windows says the cable’s network is “Public”, make it private.

data.name: Guida_NonSiCollega7
data.value: Still nothing? Open “FAQ”, use the QR code, or “Report a bug”.

data.name: Domanda_NonTrova
data.value: The phone can’t find the computer

data.name: Risposta_NonTrova
data.value: Open WebcamLR on the computer. Check that the phone and computer are on the same Wi-Fi network (not the “guest” one). On the iPhone: Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › WebcamLR on. If it still doesn’t show up, use the computer’s QR code or the USB cable.

data.name: Risposta_ReteLocale
data.value: It’s the permission iOS asks for on the iPhone to look for computers in your home. Without it, WebcamLR can’t see the computer. Turn it on in Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network. WebcamLR doesn’t use the network for anything else.

data.name: Domanda_ReteOspiti
data.value: It won’t connect at a hotel, office or school

data.name: Risposta_ReteOspiti
data.value: Many public networks keep devices apart: they’re online but can’t talk to each other. Use the USB cable, or turn on the phone’s hotspot (on the iPhone, “Personal Hotspot”) and connect the computer to it.

data.name: Domanda_Cavo
data.value: How do I connect with the USB cable?

data.name: Risposta_Cavo
data.value: With an iPhone: plug it into the computer with the cable and open WebcamLR on both; the connection starts by itself and “USB cable” appears at the top. On Windows you need the free “Apple Devices” app from the Microsoft Store. If you’re already connected over Wi-Fi, the video moves to the cable by itself, without stopping; if you unplug the cable it goes back to Wi-Fi. With Android: plug in the cable, turn on “USB tethering” on the phone (Settings › Hotspot & tethering) and choose the computer, or use the QR code; on the Mac it only works with some phones. The cable is the most stable choice and charges the phone at the same time.

data.name: Domanda_Codice
data.value: Why does the computer ask me for a code?

data.name: Risposta_Codice
data.value: It’s the first time that phone connects. Check that the 4 digits are the same on the phone and on the computer, then choose “Allow”. From then on it connects without asking. With the QR code no code is needed.

data.name: Domanda_Identita
data.value: “The computer’s identity has changed”: what does it mean?

data.name: Risposta_Identita
data.value: The phone remembers every computer it has used. If a computer with the same name shows up different, the phone stops for safety. This happens if you reinstalled WebcamLR on the computer: connect again with the QR code. If you didn’t change anything, don’t connect.

data.name: Risposta_Ritardo
data.value: Look at the indicator at the top: “Excellent”, “Good” or “Weak”. With “Weak”, move closer to the router, use the 5 GHz network, stop downloads, or use the USB cable. Wi-Fi Direct, if turned on on the Mac, can make latency less stable: turn it off if you don’t need it.

data.name: Domanda_ZoomTeams
data.value: Zoom, Teams or Meet don’t see WebcamLR

data.name: Risposta_ZoomTeams
data.value: In the app’s video settings choose “WebcamLR” as the camera: it works in any app, from Zoom to Teams, Meet, FaceTime and OBS. If it isn’t there, quit and reopen the call app after opening WebcamLR. On the Mac you need the version with the virtual webcam (coming soon: it requires an Apple developer account); on Windows it’s already there, with WebcamLR’s virtual webcam. For the phone’s microphone: on the Mac choose “WebcamLR (microphone)”; on Windows it goes through a virtual audio cable (for example VB-CABLE), and in the app you choose “CABLE Output”.

data.name: Risposta_Caldo
data.value: It’s normal during long calls. WebcamLR darkens the screen after 30 seconds and, if the phone gets very hot, lowers the quality by itself and tells you. Take off the case, keep the phone out of the sun and, if you can, don’t charge it during the call.

data.name: Risposta_Batteria
data.value: Below 20% without a charger, WebcamLR switches to 24 frames per second to last longer. For long calls plug in the charger, or the USB cable to the computer, which charges and sends video at the same time.

data.name: Domanda_Nero
data.value: The video is black on the computer

data.name: Risposta_Nero
data.value: Wait a few seconds: the video starts from the first complete frame. On Windows, if you chose HEVC on the phone, you need “HEVC Video Extensions” from the Microsoft Store: otherwise choose H.264 in the phone’s settings.

data.name: Risposta_Firewall
data.value: On first launch Windows asks for network permission: allow it for private networks. Also check that the PC’s network is “Private” (Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi › properties). With Android USB tethering the same goes for the cable’s network, in Network & internet › Ethernet. With the iPhone cable the firewall doesn’t matter.

data.name: Domanda_Qualita
data.value: How do I get the best quality?

data.name: Risposta_Qualita
data.value: Put the phone sideways on a stand, use the back camera (it’s the best one), good light in front of you and the USB cable or 5 GHz Wi-Fi. In Settings you can choose resolution and frame rate.

data.name: Domanda_Privacy
data.value: Does my video go over the internet?

data.name: Risposta_Privacy
data.value: No. The video goes from the phone to the computer only over your network or the cable, encrypted with new keys for every connection. WebcamLR has no required accounts, doesn’t record and doesn’t collect data.

data.name: Domanda_Aggiorna
data.value: “Update WebcamLR on the computer”: what should I do?

data.name: Risposta_Aggiorna
data.value: The computer has an old version of WebcamLR that doesn’t use the encrypted connection yet. Download the latest version from the WebcamLR website and install it over the old one: your phones are kept. Then reopen WebcamLR on both.

data.name: Risposta_Costo
data.value: Yes: the free version stays free forever, up to 720p at 30 fps, with no watermark, no ads and no account. WebcamLR Pro is a one-time purchase, with no subscription: €14.99 (the price may vary by country and store), and it adds 1080p, 4K, 60 fps, effects and Pro controls. You buy it on the phone, from the App Store or Google Play, and it also unlocks the connected computer: there’s nothing to buy on the Mac or on Windows.
